rationale: This is essentially a repackaged value-plus-financial-strength screen (Piotroski/Altman-style quality-value composites are long published), and the nested SUMRANK arbitrarily assigns B/M a 50% weight versus 25% each to the solvency legs without any stated justification, so it is more a known-anomaly blend than a testable cross-theme interaction.

The sign-flip on three-year smoothed earnings is a genuine interaction rather than a linear control and maps cleanly to the value-trap story, though it is close in spirit to known profitability-conditioned value and the raw unranked B/M ratio (plus negative-ceq firms, which get flipped twice) will make the Fama-MacBeth slope outlier-sensitive.
EBITDA-to-enterprise-value is the published enterprise multiple anomaly (Loughran-Wellman 2011) verbatim, and it is a single ratio with no cross-theme interaction at all.

Internally inconsistent: the reasoning claims "firms with no debt retain their full sales-yield score," but with dltt+dlc = 0 the coverage ratio is undefined and those firms will be dropped or mis-gated, and the underlying sales-to-price leg is itself a long-published value anomaly attached to a lossy hard 0/1 switch.

The expected negative sign fights the expression's dominant loading — the product of two positive ranks is monotone increasing in B/M, so the signal will largely inherit the positive value premium — and the low end of a rank product is an ambiguous mixture of cheap-unlevered and expensive-levered firms, making the short leg economically ill-defined and the construct close to the known distress anomaly.

Conditioning the value discount on the direction rather than the level of leverage is a defensible and reasonably distinct mechanism, but the unranked product will be dominated by the magnitude of the noisy annual leverage change rather than by cheapness, so a rank-by-rank or sign-gated version would likely be needed for the portfolio evidence to be stable.
